Alex.confusing: The Eagle's wording ("lay an egg for every visitor they had") was easy to misread, and the table argued for several rounds over whether its gains come from visitors to the Eagle or to its target. Confusion over the Turkey, which pays the visitor, added to it.
Alex.fun: Round 1's day, where the table cross-checked the Falcon, Eagle, and Owl reports against each other and Blair's Turkey defense briefly flipped the suspicion. It felt like real deduction.
Alex.change: Make the Eagle and Turkey rules unambiguous, and have dawn reports say which visits paid the nest, so players spend less time arguing over the mechanics.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I gave two different visit stories (Casey, then Finley), which made my Meowfia Sphinx look like the liar. I should have stuck to one story, Finley, and defended it without pushing Blair so hard.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle rule ("lays an egg for every visitor they had") was ambiguous: several players, including me, argued over whether the gains come from visitors to the Eagle or to its target, and the table never settled it. The Turkey's "pays the visitor" wording also caused a lot of early confusion.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was a blast: the table spent a whole day arguing over whether a Turkey egg or an Eagle gain was a lie, and Finley's Eagle +2 turned into the vote that eggsecuted them. My Meowfia side won that round, and the Grudge doubling my 3-card throw felt great.
Blair.change: Spell out the Eagle and Turkey rules in plain words on the role cards, so players can check egg counts without arguing about the wording. Also consider making the Sphinx's and Mouser's information clearer, since their reports were hard to verify.
Blair.regret: In round 2, as a Farm Eagle, I threw my single card at Casey, who was Farm, instead of at Drew, who was Meowfia, and I kept insisting on my own reading of the Eagle rule instead of asking the table to check it. I would throw at the player the evidence pointed to and admit when the rule was unclear.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's wording was easy to misread: several players, including me at first, thought its egg gains came from visiting its target rather than from visitors to the Eagle itself. The Storyteller's stake and banking rules were also hard to track across a round.
Casey.fun: Round 1 went well: I was the Sphinx with Blair, and the table's Turkey and Eagle claims kept colliding, so every Farm claim got tested. Finley's eggsecution, where my double-banked stake paid off, was satisfying.
Casey.change: I'd make the Eagle and Turkey wording unambiguous and show the day's egg-change reasons, so players spend less time arguing over rules instead of roles.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw my cards at Blair, who was Farm, when Drew and Finley were the Meowfia. Knowing that, I'd have thrown at Drew, since Alex's Hawk read pointed there and Drew's visit story never fit.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's payout rule was easy to misread: several of us, myself included, first read it as gaining eggs from our own visit rather than from visitors to our target. That confusion drove a lot of wrong accusations.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when Blair's Eagle claim fell apart and the table voted Blair out, while I had secretly been Meowfia with Finley and banked my cards at double value.
Drew.change: Make the role text for each animal clearer about who gains eggs and from whom, especially the Eagle and Turkey, so players stop misreading their own payouts.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I threw at Finley with a card and sided with Ellis, and in Round 3 I backed the Alex vote; I'd have been more careful about checking the Eagle rule before accusing Blair and Finley. Knowing Finley was actually Farm and Blair was Meowfia, I'd have pushed harder on Blair early.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was easy to misread: several players, me included, thought it paid for visiting the Eagle's target rather than for visitors to the Eagle. The Turkey's pay-the-visitor rule caused a similar mix-up early on.
Ellis.fun: Watching the table reason through the Owl, Falcon, Turkey and Eagle claims, and catching Blair and Finley repeating the same wrong Eagle count, was the most engaging part.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports name the visitors and the rule that applied, so players can check claims without parsing the animal text.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Finley, a Farm player, based on a misread Eagle count. Knowing the Eagle rule, I would have checked the count first and held a Wild rather than accusing Finley.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule, since the table, including me, kept misreading whether gains come from visitors to the Eagle or to its target. The text "learn which players visited them" was ambiguous.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when my Hawk visit to Ellis showed an egg and I called it out, the table split and Ellis's Meowfia side was confirmed at the vote.
Finley.change: Make the Eagle and Turkey wording unambiguous about who pays whom, since most of the day went to misreading those two roles.
Finley.regret: I publicly revealed my Hawk result on the first beat of round 3, and I collapsed soon after, likely to a Wink. I would hold the Hawk claim until the vote so Ellis's team had less time to act on it.
